title: Truly this man (Mark 15:21–47)
hook: Simon carries the cross, the centurion says Indeed this man was the son of God
tomorrow: Camp 4 close: he goes before you

segments.voice: Yesterday, the crown: purple, thorns, and soldiers kneeling in mockery. Today, one of those soldiers sees something.

Roman soldiers grab a man coming in from the countryside and force him to carry a condemned man's cross. His name is Simon, from Cyrene, in North Africa. Mark adds that he was the father of Alexander and Rufus, as if his readers knew them. Maybe they did. Maybe carrying that cross changed a family. And at the end of the road, at Golgotha, the place of the skull, a Roman officer will say the sentence Mark has been building toward since his first line.
screen: `SIMON OF CYRENE, GRABBED.` → `THE FATHER OF ALEXANDER AND RUFUS.` → `GOLGOTHA, THE PLACE OF THE SKULL.`

segments.voice: First, the cross. They crucify him at the third hour, between two thieves. Over him, the charge: the King of the Jews. Passersby, priests, even the men crucified beside him mock him: he saved others, himself he cannot save. They're right, in a way they don't understand. Second, the cry. From the sixth hour darkness covers the land until the ninth. Jesus cries out in Aramaic, and Mark keeps the words: "Eloi, Eloi, lamma sabacthani? Which is, being interpreted, My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?" It's the first line of Psalm 21 in the Douay, 22 in most Bibles, a psalm this path met in camp four, which begins in abandonment and ends in praise. With a loud cry, he dies. The veil of the Temple is torn in two, top to bottom. Third, the soldier. Mark began his Gospel calling Jesus the Son of God. A voice from heaven has said it. Demons have shouted it. But in Mark, no human being has said it and meant it, until now. The centurion facing the cross sees how he died, and says: "Indeed this man was the son of God." A Roman, a Gentile, the officer in charge of the execution. Fourth, who stayed. The men have all fled. But women were watching from a distance: Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James and Joseph, Salome, and many others who had followed him from Galilee. Then Joseph of Arimathea, a respected council member, goes boldly to Pilate, asks for the body, wraps it in linen, lays it in a tomb cut from rock, and rolls a stone across the door.
screen: `HE SAVED OTHERS, HIMSELF HE CANNOT.` · `MY GOD, MY GOD: PSALM 21 [22].` · `A ROMAN SOLDIER SAYS IT.` · `THE WOMEN STAYED.` · then, large: `INDEED THIS MAN WAS THE SON OF GOD.`

segments.voice: Simon didn't choose that cross; it was put on his shoulders on an ordinary day. Think of someone near you carrying something heavy right now, an illness, a move, a sick parent, a lot of work, a grief, and picture one piece of it you could carry for a while: a meal, an errand, an hour, a text that says I'm thinking of you. If you pray, you can pray for them by name.
Centurion. The Roman officer at the cross who says, indeed this man was the son of God. Today's word.
Your line: the soldier saw. At the cross, he saw what others missed. Day two hundred thirty, done.

howItsDone: Catholics walk the fourteen Stations of the Cross, especially on Fridays in Lent, where Simon of Cyrene helps Jesus carry the cross at the fifth station, and on Good Friday the passion is read aloud and the faithful venerate the cross.

chat.says: In Mark, who is the first person to call Jesus the Son of God at the cross?
options: A Roman centurion, the officer at the execution, who saw how he died.
Peter, who came back to the cross after weeping by the fire.
The women watching from a distance, who said it to each other.
chat.meaning: In Mark no human says it and means it until the centurion, a Gentile, sees how Jesus died: indeed this man was the son of God.

centurion.meaning: an officer in the Roman army

Cyrene.meaning: a city in North Africa, Simon's home

Golgotha.meaning: the place of the skull, where Jesus was crucified

Joseph of Arimathea.meaning: a council member who buried Jesus

notes: Douay-Rheims Mark 15:34 and 15:39 given from memory; confirm spelling of 'lamma sabacthani' in Challoner.

'The first human in Mark to say it and mean it': Peter says 'the Christ' (8:29) and the high priest asks 'the Son of the blessed' (14:61), but no human confesses 'Son of God' before 15:39. Confirm. The textual question over 'Son of God' in 1:1 is not raised.
The reading of Psalm 22 as ending in praise, so that the cry evokes the whole psalm, is a traditional reading; confirm framing.
Alexander and Rufus perhaps known to Mark's readers (cf. Romans 16:13): stated as 'maybe'.
Simon at the fifth station: confirm.
